place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房 · 开春

setup.zh: 正月里，家里的回信到了。开了春，周衡那一篮残株送到了。
setup.en: In the first month the letter from home came. In spring, Zhou Heng's basket of culls arrives.

recap.zh: 开春的残株一株一株喂进饭桶，开出三颗聚气丹——一纹、二纹、九纹各一；分堆一认，认出三张方子——方子管出什么丹，纹是运气；缸是饭桶涨的，层是崖顶上定风过的，一个月过了五层；灵石先见了底。阿禾、孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包：二狗的二纹，阿禾的那一颗九纹。
recap.en: The spring culls went into the Rice Tub one by one and gave three qi pills — one ring, two rings and nine; sorted into heaps, they gave up three recipes — a recipe decides the pill, the rings are luck; the Rice Tub filled the jar, the layer was crossed on the clifftop by stilling the wind, past five within the month; the spirit stones ran out first. Under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's, an oilpaper packet each: Ergou's the two-ring, A-He's the nine.

en: The letter from home: the roof is mended.
A basket of culls, thrown out.

story.zh: 正月里，家里的回信到了。坊市逢十九有集，蒙山来的信客在钱掌柜的摊子边上支一张小桌，收信，交信；他的家信，走的都是这张小桌。他娘的字小，写得密：屋顶修了；五两银子腊月里送到了，你爹便再没往黑松岭那头去过。末了一句是：吴婆婆让我捎一句话给你，她说：「告诉那孩子，牙还在。」我问她什么牙，她不说，只是笑。
story.en: In the first month the reply from home arrived. The market held a fair on every nineteenth, and the letter-carrier from Mengshan set up a little table beside Shopkeeper Qian's stall, taking letters and handing them out; every letter from home came over that little table. His mother's hand was small and close: the roof was mended; the five taels had come in the twelfth month, and your father has not gone out toward Black Pine Ridge since. The last line was: Granny Wu asked me to pass you a message. She said: "Tell the boy, the tooth is still there." I asked her what tooth; she wouldn't say, only smiled.

exits.means: feeds the spring culls into the Rice Tub: three qi pills of one, two and nine rings, the two-ring to 孙二狗 and the nine to 阿禾; sorts the basket by herb and finds the three recipes (黄精+灵石 → 聚气丹, 黄芪+a breath → 回春丹, 紫玉参+a breath → 回气丹) — the recipe decides the pill, the grade is luck (mostly one or two rings, 2026-10-07); the jar fills on pills, 五层 is crossed on the cliff (定风), 灵石 run out before 黄精

story.zh:
好容易熬到开了春，药园开了园。月底他拿巡夜簿去执事堂交了差——东墙的差事，月底都是周衡坐在东墙底下收簿子、发工钱——周衡翻了翻簿子，在账上记了一笔，把一篮残株推了过来，巡夜牌上写着的工钱：黄精的烂根，黄芪的虫叶，当归的歪苗，篮底还压着两根紫玉参的断须。他差不多全拿去喂了饭桶，开出来的大半是灰和烟，没一点用处；他也不心疼，只当是摸它的脾气，喂一株，记一株，记着记着，觉得自己慢慢摸着一点饭桶的门道了。半个月喂下去半篮，开出三颗[聚气丹]{注=qi-pill}，青白透亮。三颗一个样子，纹却不一样：一颗一道纹，跟外门份例里每月那一颗一般；一颗两道纹；还有一颗，他对着柴房门缝里的光数了三遍，九道。

他爹说，打猎靠的不是运气，是脚印。他把剩下的半篮按样分成四堆，蹲着把这半个月的脚印一个一个往回认，认了一夜，认出三张方子：黄精搭一块灵石，出聚气丹；黄芪搭一口自己的气，出回春丹；紫玉参的断须搭一口气，出回气丹，丹田空了吞一颗，一口气灌回来大半缸。乱搭的，仍旧是灰。方子管的是出什么丹，不管出几道纹：同一根黄精，同一块灵石，这一回一道，下一回两道，隔上好几个月，才蹦出一颗三道四道的。九道的，开春那一颗之后，他再没见过第二颗。方子他一个字也没往纸上写，记在肚里。

打这以后，饭桶吐一颗聚气丹，他便吃一颗；一道纹的，丹田里那口缸涨一指，两道纹的，涨一指半。可缸涨了，层不涨。层是在崖顶上过的。他照师父的功课，每天天不亮上崖顶，站到巽那一格上，看落叶打转。头一个月，叶子转，他的眼睛跟着转；第二个月，他的眼睛不转了，叶子还转；到了三月里一个早上，一片叶子从崖边起来，往他脸上飘，他没躲，也没砍，只往旁边挪了半步——那片叶子贴着他的耳朵飘过去了。他看见了它起来的那一下。那天早上，丹田里那口缸「咚」地一沉，他过了五层。下一回上崖顶，他把这一下说给师父听，瞿老道：「定风。」缸是饭桶替他涨的，层是他自己过的——靠这饭桶的丹药，沈小满进步神速。只有一样不省事：黄精月月有，灵石月月见底——份例十块，一颗丹搭一块，不到半个月便喂空了。他站在执事堂西墙底下，看那些写着「灵石」的牌子，头一回觉得那不是牌子，是丹。

过了两日，讲堂上阿禾和孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包，包里一颗聚气丹。小满只说是利息：孙二狗那一颗，是牛棚里那半张饼的，两道纹；阿禾那一颗，他没说——是那颗九道的。旁人问起来路，小满便说是秘境里捡的：潭边一个死人，袋子里有一只瓶。

阿禾把那颗丹对着窗户的光转了一圈，嘴唇一动一动的，是在数纹。数到第九道，她的嘴唇停住了。她什么也没问，原样包好，揣进怀里，没有吃。

孙二狗却当夜就吃了。天亮的时候，孙二狗从练气零层，冲到了一层。他站在大通铺门口，把一只手摊在太阳底下，瞧着掌心里那一缕细细的黄气，瞧得眼泪鼻涕一齐流了下来。褚先生说过，伪灵根引气，五年起步；他进山门才半年。说书的替他算一笔账：这半年，他夜夜蹲在柴堆上数气，那口枯井底下，早磨出了一点潮；两道纹的丹，是往那点潮上浇了一瓢水。瓢是小满的，井是他自己一夜一夜挖的。

这一哭，哭坏了事。一个零层的伪灵根，一夜引了气，不到晌午便传遍了外门，天黑前传进了内门。
story.en:
At last spring came, and the herb garden opened. At the month's end he took the night-watch book to the Hall of Errands to hand in the job — the east wall's chores are settled there at every month's end, Zhou Heng sitting under the east wall taking in the books and paying the wages — and Zhou Heng leafed through the book, made a note in his ledger and pushed a basket of culls across: the pay written on the night-watch tag. Rotten Solomon's-seal roots, worm-eaten astragalus leaves, crooked angelica seedlings, and at the bottom two broken root-hairs of purple jade ginseng. Nearly all of it went to the Rice Tub, and what came out was mostly ash and smoke, no use at all; he didn't grudge it, only took it as learning the thing's temper — one fed, one remembered — and bit by bit he felt he was getting a feel for the Rice Tub. Half a month took half the basket and gave three qi pills, clear as pale jade. Three of a kind to look at, but the rings differed: one had a single ring, like the outer court's monthly allowance pill; one had two; and the third — he counted it three times against the light through the woodshed door — had nine.

His father used to say hunting runs on tracks, not luck. He sorted the rest of the basket into four heaps by kind and squatted there reading the half-month's tracks back one by one; a night of it, and he had three recipes. Solomon's seal with a spirit stone gave a qi pill; astragalus with one breath of his own qi gave a mending pill; a purple jade ginseng root-hair with one breath gave a qi-restoring pill — dantian run dry, swallow one, and most of the jar came back in a single breath. Anything mixed was still ash. A recipe decided what pill came out, not how many rings: the same root, the same stone, one ring this time and two the next, and only once in several months a three or a four. A nine — after that first one in spring he never saw a second. He never put a word of the recipes on paper; he kept them in his head.

From then on, whenever the Rice Tub gave a qi pill, he ate it; a one-ring pill raised the jar in his dantian a finger's width, a two-ring one a finger and a half. But the jar rose and the layer did not. Layers were crossed on the clifftop. He kept his master's homework: up the cliff before light every day, onto the Xun square, watching the fallen leaves turn. The first month the leaves turned and his eyes turned with them; the second month his eyes stopped and the leaves went on; then one morning in the third month a leaf came up off the cliff edge straight at his face, and he did not duck and did not cut, only shifted half a step aside — and the leaf brushed past his ear. He had seen the moment it rose. That morning the jar in his dantian settled with a thump, and he was past layer five. The next time he went up he told his master about that moment. Old Qu said: "Stilling the wind." The Rice Tub filled the jar for him; the layers he crossed himself — on the Rice Tub's pills, Shen Xiaoman advanced by leaps and bounds. Only one thing was not spared him: Solomon's seal came every month, and spirit stones ran out every month — ten in the allowance, one to a pill, and they were fed away in under half a month. He stood under the west wall of the Hall of Errands, looking at the tags that said *spirit stones*, and for the first time saw not tags but pills.

Two days later, under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's in the lecture hall, there was an oilpaper packet each, a qi pill inside. Xiaoman said only that it was interest: Sun Ergou's on half a flatbread in the cowshed — the two-ring one; A-He's, he didn't say — it was the nine. When others asked where they came from, Xiaoman said he had picked them up in the secret realm: a dead man by the pool, a bottle in his bag.

A-He turned the pill once in the light from the window, her lips moving — counting rings. At the ninth her lips stopped. She asked nothing, wrapped it up as it was, tucked it into her jacket, and did not eat it.

Sun Ergou ate his that very night. At daybreak, Sun Ergou broke from Qi Condensation layer zero to layer one. He stood at the dormitory door with one hand held open in the sun, looking at the thin yellow wisp of qi in his palm, until tears and snot ran down together. Master Chu had said a false root takes five years at the least to draw in qi; he had been inside the gate half a year. The storyteller will do his sums for him: that half year, every night squatting on the woodpile counting breaths, and the bottom of that dry well had already sweated a little damp; two rings of a pill were a ladle of water poured on that damp. The ladle was Xiaoman's; the well he had dug himself, night after night.

That crying spoiled everything. A false-root boy at layer zero drawing in qi in a single night — before noon the whole outer court knew it, and by dark the inner court too.
